public_rationale: The contract asks whether at least two million people were angry at Altman or OpenAI over the Pentagon deal between February 27 and March 7, 2026. Sensor Tower reported that US ChatGPT uninstalls rose 295% day over day on February 28, 2026, against a 30-day average of 9% (e3). It gave no absolute numbers. On March 4, Business Today, citing The Times, reported that about 1.5 million people had signed up to the QuitGPT campaign (e2). That figure is below two million. On March 5, Fox 5 reported QuitGPT's own claim of more than 2.5 million people (e1). That count includes cancellations, pledges and social media shares. The packet has no independent check of it. The packet has no independent absolute count and no representative poll of anger at OpenAI or Altman. It also has no figures showing the backlash stayed below a million. The evidence shows a measurable backlash but does not show its size.
limitations: Anger and betrayal are not measured directly. Boycott sign-ups and uninstalls are proxies that may reflect other motives.
The only figures in the millions are the campaign's own count or reports of it. The 2.5 million figure includes social media shares.
Sensor Tower gives only percentage changes in US uninstalls, not totals.
One poll on AI companies and military use could not be read (HTTP 429). It reportedly measured alignment with Anthropic versus the Pentagon, not anger at OpenAI.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Millions of people are angry and many feel betrayed by Altman/OpenAI.

statement.excerpt: Millions of people, literally, are angry; many feel betrayed.
statement.document_title: BREAKING: Sam Altman’s greed and dishonesty are finally catching up to him

our_interpretation: Plain reading: at least two million people were angry at Altman or OpenAI over the Pentagon deal around the post date, and a substantial number felt betrayed.
Acceptable evidence is a reliable count of people taking protest actions (cancellations, uninstalls, pledges) or representative polling showing anger at OpenAI at that scale.
Target period: February 27 to March 7, 2026, from the deal announcement to the post date.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable, preferably independent, figures show millions of people protesting or reporting anger at OpenAI/Altman over the deal.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable figures show the backlash was limited to thousands or hundreds of thousands of people.

evidence.excerpt: An organization called QuitGPT claims that as of this week, more than 2.5 million people have either canceled their ChatGPT subscriptions, pledged to stop using the app or shared news of their boycott on social media.
evidence.explanation: A million-scale figure, but it is the campaign's own unverified claim and counts social media shares as well as cancellations.

evidence.excerpt: In response, a “Quit GPT” campaign began online, and about 1.5 million people reportedly signed up to support it.
evidence.explanation: An earlier reported figure of 1.5 million sign-ups. It is 'reportedly', not independently verified, and below two million.

evidence.excerpt: In contrast, ChatGPT has only averaged a 9% DoD uninstall rate over the past 30 days.
evidence.explanation: Independent data confirm an unusual uninstall spike (295% day-over-day against a 9% norm). But they give no absolute numbers, so they cannot show 'millions'.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: An independent absolute count of ChatGPT cancellations, uninstalls or protest actions between February 27 and March 7, 2026, or a representative poll measuring anger at OpenAI or Altman over the deal. Either would need to show a total of at least two million to support the claim, or a total in the thousands or hundreds of thousands to contradict it.
